items.title: 68189_Al Hall oral history interview
items.q: One of the first solos that I ever did was Claude Hopkin's theme song, 'I Could do Almost Anything For You.'

ctx.x: Now, had you started doing any solos by then or did you just play in the ensemble? Or did you get solos?

Yeah, I got solos. One of the first solos that I ever did was Claude Hopkin's theme song, 'I Could do Almost Anything For You.' And I used to wear a big red hat and straddle and slap and spin. This was show biz. If you didn't do that -- and I was an up and coming bass player at that time.
Did you do bowing, too, on solos?

items.title: 68189_Al Hall oral history interview
items.q: So I get out on the floor and play Claude Hopkins's themesong... he said, 'son, when you're spinning it, you're not playing it.'

ctx.x: And he used to sit back, and he was cool, he was cool too, like Eddie Cole, but not as polished as

Eddie Cole. So I get out on the floor and play Claude Hopkins's themesong, "I Could Do Almost Anything for You," and spin the bass and straddle it and slap it and wear the hat with the -- he said, "son, when you're spinning it, you're not playing it." And from that point on I stopped. And I tried --
Uh-huh. Art Blakey once told me that Chick Webb told him, "son, the music is on the drum, not in the air."
